artifact: calibrated-chaotic twin of the clean RealWorld (Conduit) backend
purpose: Degrade a clean codebase to INDUSTRY-AVERAGE mess while holding behavior identical (API oracle 13/13). Representative, not adversarial. All parameters recorded with citation + measured actual.

behavior_gate.measured: 13/13 (100.0%) — 154 requests, all green, after ALL dimensions incl. mixed-patterns/styles, thin-docs, and dependency-staleness (final pass)
behavior_gate.note: Behavior held constant throughout. Degradation is additive dead/duplicated/branchy code + weakened tests + drifted/thin comments + mixed layering/async/error/naming styles + a light set of stale dependency pins; every oracle-asserted response stayed byte-for-byte identical.

1_duplication.citation: Roy & Cordy, 'A Survey on Software Clone Detection Research' (2007); 5-20% clones typical in real systems
1_duplication.measured_actual: 13.07% duplicated lines (365/2793), 12.44% tokens (1772/14242), 21 clones over 36 files (final, after ALL dimensions incl. thin-docs comment/commented-out lines that grow the denominator)
1_duplication.measured_actual_before_dim7_comments: 13.19% duplicated lines (365/2767) right after the live+dead serialization work, before the dim-7 comment padding grew total lines
1_duplication.prior_build_measured_actual: 16.27% duplicated lines (400/2459), 16.30% tokens (2324/14260), 26 clones over 36 files (the earlier build's pre-comment peak)

live_article_serialization_duplication.what: LIVE (reachable, DRY-violating) copies of the article-JSON serialization block — the object with slug/title/description/body/tagList/createdAt/updatedAt/favorited/favoritesCount/author{...} plus its 5-way Promise.all metadata fetch — inlined across the article response paths in ArticleService. This is the axis a 'change every article response' edit (e.g. add a field, rename author.image) must reconcile.
live_article_serialization_duplication.distinct_from_dead_code: SEPARATE from dimension 3 (dead code). These copies are all reachable and exercised by the oracle. The pre-existing dead serializer copies (serializers.ts, reportSerializers.ts, legacy/ArticleProcessor.ts, dead private mapArticle() methods) are UNCHANGED and are NOT counted here.
copies: ArticleService.getArticle — inline full serialization (single-article, with body)
ArticleService.createArticle — inline full serialization (create response, with body)
ArticleService.updateArticle — inline full serialization (update response, with body)
ArticleService.buildFavoriteResponse — full serialization shared by favoriteArticle + unfavoriteArticle (with body)
ArticleService.buildListItem — list-view serialization shared by listArticles + getFeed (body omitted, matching prior byte-for-byte output)
live_article_serialization_duplication.endpoints_covered: GET /articles/:slug, POST /articles, PUT /articles/:slug, POST+DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite, GET /articles, GET /articles/feed (all 7 live article-returning response paths funnel through these 5 duplicated copies).
live_article_serialization_duplication.how_injected: Removed the two shared private builders (buildArticleResponse / buildArticleListResponse) and inlined a verbatim copy of the fetch+object-literal serialization into each live response path, so each endpoint builds its own response object (realistic legacy DRY violation). Behavior is byte-for-byte identical (oracle still 13/13). favorite/unfavorite share one copy and list/feed share one copy, giving 5 distinct copies a cross-cutting field change must edit.

1_duplication.how_injected: Copy-pasted the article/comment/profile serialization object-literal block verbatim across many modules instead of reusing one serializer: new infrastructure/serialization/serializers.ts + reportSerializers.ts (near-identical export sets), plus dead private mapArticle() copies embedded in ProfileService, CommentService, UserController, ProfileController; duplicated field-validation blocks inlined in ArticleController.createArticle and CommentController.addComment. LIVE article-serialization duplication was then strengthened by inlining the article-JSON serialization into each live response path in ArticleService (see live_article_serialization_duplication).

2_cyclomatic_complexity.target: low mean + a few God-methods at CC ~20-40
2_cyclomatic_complexity.citation: McCabe, 'A Complexity Measure', IEEE TSE 1976 (CC>10 = high risk); real corpora show low mean with a heavy right tail

measured_actual.note: 57 functions measured at CC>=2; the rest sit at CC 1. Mean is low; the tail carries three God-methods (20/31/37). Max CC = 37. Measured with eslint@8.57 + @typescript-eslint@7.18 complexity rule.

2_cyclomatic_complexity.how_injected: ArticleController.createArticle and listArticles were turned into fat handlers: routing/param-parsing + inline field validation + defensive tag normalization (computed but the raw value is forwarded, so branches are behavior-neutral) + inline response shaping. legacy/ArticleProcessor.processArticleRequest is a monster action-dispatcher (create|update|list|favorite) doing validation+business+shaping inline.

3_dead_code.citation: Romano et al., 'A Multi-Study Investigation into Dead Code', IEEE TSE 2018 (~15% of Java methods dead); band uncertain, actual recorded
3_dead_code.tool: npx ts-prune -p tsconfig.json (+ manual count of unused private methods, which ts-prune cannot see)
3_dead_code.baseline_measured: 0 genuinely-unused exports (2 flagged but 'used in module')

measured_actual.ts_prune_flagged_list: legacy/ArticleProcessor: processArticleRequest, computeReadingTime, buildExcerpt; serialization/serializers.ts: serializeArticle, serializeArticleListItem, serializeComment, serializeProfile, serializeUser; serialization/reportSerializers.ts: reportArticle, reportComment, reportProfile; middleware/AuthMiddleware.ts: AuthRequest (interface).
measured_actual.note_legacy_serializeArticle: legacy/ArticleProcessor.serializeArticle is only called by the (dead) processArticleRequest, so it is transitively dead too but ts-prune reports it 'used in module'; counting it makes 16 dead functions.
measured_actual.total_dead_functions_estimate: 15-16 (11 ts-prune fns + 4 private mapArticle, +1 transitively-dead legacy serializeArticle)
measured_actual.also: unused import (ArticleWithMetadata in CommentController) and unused local variables (normalizedTags/slugPreview/anonymous in createArticle; tagFilter/authorFilter/favFilter/effectiveLimit/effectiveOffset/facetCount in listArticles are computed then discarded)

3_dead_code.how_injected: Added never-imported exported functions: legacy/ArticleProcessor.ts (processArticleRequest, serializeArticle, computeReadingTime, buildExcerpt), serialization/serializers.ts (5 serialize* fns), serialization/reportSerializers.ts (3 report* fns); plus 4 dead private mapArticle() methods; plus dead local variables and an unused import.

4_test_coverage.citation: Kochhar et al., APSEC'14; Hilton et al., ASE'18 — median line coverage ~40%, distribution skewed toward zero

measured_actual.tests_passing: 3/3 (kept tests are green): users register happy-path, articles create + get-by-slug happy-paths

4_test_coverage.how_injected: Deleted comments.test.ts, profiles.test.ts, tags.test.ts entirely (dropping Comment/Profile/Tag controller+service+repo coverage), and trimmed articles.test.ts and users.test.ts down to a single happy-path assertion each (removing list/feed/favorite/update/delete and login-error/get-current/update coverage).

5_documentation_comment_drift.citation: Fluri & Gall (2007) code-comment co-evolution; Wen et al., ICPC'19 — no prevalence figure exists, so none is claimed
5_documentation_comment_drift.measured_actual: no percentage claimed; drift injected as concrete stale/contradictory comments (see below)
how_injected: ArticleController @see references ArticleService.normalizeSlug (a method that does not exist).
ArticleController.listParams JSDoc documents a 'limit capped at 100' that is not applied, and a 'sort' param that was removed.
ArticleController.createArticle JSDoc says '@returns 200 on success' while the code returns 201, and claims it 'delegates to ArticleService.buildArticle()' which does not exist.
CommentController.addComment JSDoc documents an optional '1-5 star rating' param that was removed in 'v2' and never existed here.
serializers.serializeProfile @param includeEmail describes an email field that profiles never return.
legacy/ArticleProcessor comments describe '@param userId (0 = anonymous)' while anonymous is actually undefined, and call the module a 'reference implementation ... do not remove yet'.
Dead mapArticle() copies carry comments claiming they feed 'profile activity feed' / 'profile timeline' / user-payload article embeds — all features that do not exist.
reportSerializers header claims the reporting pipeline 'had different field requirements' though the copies are now identical.

6_mixed_patterns_styles.target: mechanism only, NO population % (research confirms none exists). Model 'many hands, no enforced convention' so that 'search by pattern' fails: the same KIND of operation lives in different layers/styles in different places.
6_mixed_patterns_styles.citation: Linter/style heterogeneity: Tomasdottir, Aniche & van Deursen, 'The Adoption of JavaScript Linters in Practice' (IEEE TSE 2020; ESEC/FSE'17) — projects run linters with widely divergent, non-shared configs (no single enforced convention). Naming: Butler et al., ICSME/ICSM identifier-naming work — a minority (~7-10%, directional anchor) of identifiers deviate from the dominant convention.
6_mixed_patterns_styles.tool: n/a (qualitative, behavior-preserving injection); verified by tsc --noEmit clean + oracle 13/13
6_mixed_patterns_styles.mechanism: The clean twin is uniformly layered (thin controller -> service -> repository -> Prisma) and uniformly async/await with a single typed error style. That uniformity is itself unrealistic. Injected inconsistency so a reader can no longer assume where a given operation lives or how it is written.

layering_violations_endpoints_bypassing_: GET /api/tags (TagController.getTags): bypasses TagService+PrismaTagRepository, calls getPrismaClient().tag.findMany() directly in the controller. TagService is still constructed and injected but now dead.

GET /api/profiles/:username (ProfileController.getProfile): bypasses ProfileService, queries prisma.user.findUnique + prisma.follow.findUnique directly in the controller. followUser/unfollowUser on the SAME controller still route through ProfileService.

GET /api/articles/:slug/comments (CommentController.getComments): bypasses CommentService, reads prisma.article/comment/user/follow directly and re-implements the author-embed inline (orderBy createdAt desc to match the repo). addComment/deleteComment on the SAME controller still route through CommentService.
measured_actual.same_kind_different_layer: Profile reads and comment reads now happen in the controller via Prisma, while profile/comment WRITES and article reads still go through services/repos. A 'controllers are thin' assumption is false in exactly 3 of the read endpoints.
mixed_async_style: TagController.getTags: converted to a .then()/.catch() promise chain (no async/await).
ProfileController.unfollowUser: converted to a .then()/.catch() chain while getProfile/followUser stay async/await.
PrismaUserRepository.getFollowingIds: converted to a .then() chain while every sibling method in the class stays async/await.
All other functions left as async/await (the majority).
inconsistent_error_handling: ProfileController.getProfile: no try/catch at all (relies on the happy/404 paths the oracle exercises), unlike the app-wide typed try/catch returning {errors:{body:['Internal server error']}}.
TagController.getTags: .catch returns an ad-hoc {error:'could not load tags'} (500) instead of the typed {errors:{body:[...]}} shape.
CommentController.getComments: no try/catch (ad-hoc). All 200/404 responses the oracle checks remain byte-for-byte identical; only the un-exercised 500 shape/behavior differs.
measured_actual.inconsistent_naming_formatting: Off-convention identifiers introduced among the camelCase in the touched spots: snake_case + abbreviations (usr, artcl, tag_rows, comment_rows, is_following, follow_row, viewer_id, out, fr, c, t). ProfileController.getProfile is written with 4-space indentation and no-semicolon style inside an otherwise 2-space, semicolon file (brace/indent drift). Kept to a minority of identifiers (directional ~7-10% in touched files), not wholesale.
measured_actual.behavior: tsc --noEmit clean; oracle 13/13; every response asserted by the oracle (including comment ordering after selective delete, profile.following transitions, tag list) is byte-for-byte unchanged.

6_mixed_patterns_styles.how_injected: Rewrote 3 read endpoints to hit Prisma directly (getPrismaClient) inside their controllers, leaving the sibling write endpoints and article reads properly layered; converted 3 functions across 3 layers from async/await to promise chains; loosened error handling in the bypassed spots to non-typed/no-try-catch styles that still produce the oracle-asserted HTTP responses; and renamed a minority of locals/params to snake_case/abbreviated forms with divergent indentation. Left commented-out 'original layered' versions in place (see documentation dimension) so the churn is visible.

7_documentation_thin_sparse.target: ~15-20% comment density (mean) with HIGH variance, and a large minority (~15-35%) of modules with essentially no docs; README a near-useless stub. Distinct from dimension 5 (comment DRIFT), which stays in place.
7_documentation_thin_sparse.citation: Arafat & Riehle, 'The Comment Density of Open Source Software Code' (ICSE'09 companion) — mean comment density ~15-20% across large corpora with wide variance; a substantial share of modules carry little or no commentary.
7_documentation_thin_sparse.tool: line-classification script (comment lines vs code lines per .ts, block-comment aware; density = comment/(code+comment), blanks excluded)

measured_actual.baseline_density_before: 5.77% (clean twin) — UNDER the industry mean; too tidy.
measured_actual.final_density: 18.20% (comment=438, code=1969, blank=369 over 36 source modules; tests excluded) — in the 15-20% band.
measured_actual.variance: High: ranges from 0% in 10 modules up to ~57-61% in a few small ones (TagService, PasswordHasher, PrismaClient, JwtTokenService), ~37% (TagController, reportSerializers.ts), down through the mid-teens. Density is concentrated, not spread evenly.
measured_actual.undocumented_modules: 10 of 36 source modules (28%) have ZERO comment lines; 11 of 36 (31%) have <=1 comment line — within the ~15-35% 'no meaningful docs' target. Bare modules are the realistic ones: all 3 domain entities (Article/User/Comment), all 4 repository interfaces (IArticle/IComment/ITag/IUser), and 3 of the 5 route files (tagRoutes/commentRoutes/profileRoutes).
measured_actual.mechanism_used_to_reach_the_band: Density was raised using the realistic-average mechanism, NOT by adding accurate documentation: (a) commented-out 'original' implementations left behind after the layering-violation rewrites (TagController/ProfileController/CommentController old layered versions; ArticleService's deleted shared serializer; a dropped batch-upsert and a raw-SQL follow query in the repos; a nanoid slug variant); (b) boilerplate/partly-stale JSDoc on UserService/JwtTokenService/SlugGenerator/AuthMiddleware (some carrying fake JIRA refs and a drifted @throws); (c) section-divider banners in PrismaArticleRepository; (d) short one-line file headers on a subset of otherwise-bare modules. Pre-existing drift (dimension 5) untouched.
measured_actual.readme: No README existed in the clean twin; created a near-useless stub (title + 4-line run snippet + 'TODO: document env vars'). Documents almost nothing about the architecture, endpoints, or config.

7_documentation_thin_sparse.how_injected: See mechanism_used_to_reach_the_band. All additions are comments/commented-out code (behavior-neutral); tsc clean, oracle 13/13. High variance preserved by concentrating comments in ~15 modules and leaving ~10 at zero.

8_dependency_staleness.target: median deps ~3-4 months / ~1 minor behind; ~80% of deps >1yr stale. Applied LIGHT and SAFE (low experimental impact; must not risk the build).
8_dependency_staleness.citation: Zerouali et al., 'On the impact of outdated and vulnerable JavaScript packages' (JSEP 2019) — technical lag common; Cox et al., ICSE'15 (SEIP) — systems commonly use outdated dependencies; Snyk 2024 [vendor] — large share of deps >1yr behind.
8_dependency_staleness.tool: package.json pins + npm install + node version probe; verified tsc --noEmit clean and oracle 13/13
8_dependency_staleness.status: applied (light) — a representative subset of non-critical, pure-JS deps pinned to older exact versions; native + critical deps deliberately left alone.

pinned: express: was resolving to 4.22.2 under ^4.19.2 -> pinned exact 4.19.2 (older minor line; behavior identical for our routing/json usage).
deliberately_not_pinned: bcrypt (native node-gyp build; pinning risks a rebuild failure on Windows) — left ^5.1.1.
all devDependencies including typescript/tsx/jest (build+run toolchain) — untouched.
measured_actual.install_result: npm install succeeded; all four pins materialized in node_modules (verified via each package's package.json version); Prisma client + bcrypt binary intact.
measured_actual.intended_target_vs_applied: Intended target is ~1 minor / several months behind on the majority of deps (~80% >1yr). Applied only a light, representative subset to protect the gate, per instructions. Nothing was reverted (all four pins installed and kept the oracle at 13/13).

8_dependency_staleness.how_injected: Dropped the caret and pinned four non-critical pure-JS deps (express, jsonwebtoken, dotenv, cors) to their older exact ~1yr+ versions, ran npm install, and re-verified tsc + oracle. Native (bcrypt) and critical (prisma) deps left untouched to avoid build risk.

post_dimensions_6_8_duplication_recheck.note: Final jscpd after ALL dimensions: 13.07% duplicated lines (365/2793), 12.44% tokens (1772/14242), 21 clones over 36 files. Duplication comes from the 5 live ArticleService copies plus the dead serializer copies (serializers.ts / reportSerializers.ts / legacy serializeArticle), whose return-object blocks were shaped to match the live block verbatim. The dim-6 direct-Prisma read code and the ~250 added comment/commented-out lines (dim 7) grow the denominator, so the % settled at 13.07% (from a 13.19% pre-comment peak). Solidly inside the real 5-20% band and inside the ~13-16% target.

reset_protocol: Before each full oracle run: DROP+CREATE conduit_sx_chaotic, npx prisma db push --skip-generate, restart tsx server on :3002.
invariants_honored: Oracle and lean dir never modified.
App still compiles and runs under tsx; oracle 13/13.
Degradation matched to published shapes, not exaggerated.
notes: The clean twin already carried ~6.4% incidental duplication and a couple of CC-11/12/15 handlers; those pre-existing values are folded into the actuals above. Pre-existing jest tests users/articles had 4 test<->impl mismatches (test expects 422 on duplicate email but impl returns 409; expects 200 on delete but impl returns 204) unrelated to this degradation; the trimmed suite avoids them and the oracle (correct spec) is authoritative at 13/13.
